exposure: embryo transfer number (single, double, triple embryo transfer)
cohort: The study analyzed 6439 fresh embryo transfer women, focusing on 1647 initial singleton pregnancy patients divided into groups based on the number of embryos transferred.
finding: Single embryo transfer was associated with better perinatal outcomes, including lower rates of preterm birth and low-birth weight, and a significantly higher mean birth weight in singleton pregnancies.
birth_weight: Outcomes included low-birth weight and very low-birth weight rates; the mean delivery weight was 3440.4 g for single embryo transfer, 3320.7 g for double, and 3277.4 g for triple embryo transfer.
